raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Engram currently gathers local FP8 rows and all-reduces the BF16 result. This maps immutable shards once during loading and adds owner selection to the existing gather kernel, allowing eligible ranks to read rows directly from the owning GPU.

Support is limited to single-node SM10x TP4 / attention DP1 / CP1, verified full NVLink/P2P, standard auto/safetensors loading, and no IPC weight cache, CPU/offload backup or memory saver. Other configurations keep the existing path. Symmetric storage and its rendezvous handle remain alive for CUDA Graph replay; normal in-place reload uses the existing collective finish_load hook.

No new environment variable or registry entry is added. The final diff is 3 files, +237/-6: 125 added runtime lines and one focused 112-line distributed test. The two separate peer helper files have been removed. Final head: `99934e03ade7392ea9c6c5da97ce5349387d4077`.

### Clean serving revalidation

Baseline `779adb4b82243e7743be60a305dc62ca3bee3a3a`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, exclusive 4x GB300, TP4/EP4/attention-DP1, default auto GEMM (FlashInfer CuTeDSL), FlashMLA Mega, DSPARK5, full decode CUDA Graph. Same frozen image/model/client, real temperature-0 acceptance, fixed 512/2048 input and 256 output tokens. No loader patch, profiler during timing, simulated acceptance or launch blocking.

Eight independent starts in A/B/B/A and B/A/A/B order; each point has three measured batches per start with max(32, 8*concurrency) requests. Full-matrix and point warmup precede timing; request cache is flushed outside timing. Every measured request has zero cache hits and the requested input/output lengths; no measured batch captured a new decoder graph. All timing samples are retained. Values below are run-level geometric means, not the best batch.

| Input / output / concurrency | Baseline output tok/s | Candidate output tok/s | Change | ABBA / BAAB blocks |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 / 256 / 1 | 390.39 | 392.95 | +0.66% | +0.73% / +0.58% |
| 512 / 256 / 8 | 1214.56 | 1244.51 | +2.47% | -0.52% / +5.55% |
| 512 / 256 / 32 | 2967.66 | 3033.75 | +2.23% | +0.21% / +4.29% |
| 2048 / 256 / 1 | 362.29 | 364.65 | +0.65% | +0.20% / +1.10% |
| 2048 / 256 / 8 | 1129.94 | 1148.25 | +1.62% | -0.39% / +3.67% |
| 2048 / 256 / 32 | 2343.42 | 2371.44 | +1.20% | -1.53% / +3.99% |

A separate four-start A/B/B/A run disables speculation: 512/256 CC32: +0.06% (pairs +0.43% / -0.32%); 2048/256 CC32: +0.21% (pairs +0.88% / -0.45%). This is diagnostic and does not replace the default-mode result. Together the two protocols contain 25,088 measured requests in 176 batches. Four startup pairs still give limited precision; acceptance and same-code repeat variability are recorded, without post-hoc acceptance normalization.

### Correctness and decision

Four-rank GB300 integration tests pass for uneven/empty shards, int32/int64 IDs, invalid IDs, exponent zero, independent rank requests, zero-token lookup, changed-input graph replay, in-place reload, and dummy/IPC-cache loader fallback. Comparisons use zero numerical tolerance; no signed-zero bitwise-equivalence claim is made. The unchanged local gather also passes its external parity checks. Ruff, compile and whitespace checks pass.

GSM8K zero-shot repeats (same 200 examples, max 4096 and real EOS): 03_engram_dspark: 195/200, 04_baseline_dspark: 196/200, 07_baseline_dspark: 196/200, 08_engram_dspark: 195/200, 11_engram_nospec: 195/200, 12_baseline_nospec: 195/200. All predictions, answer changes and truncations are retained; this finite check does not prove population-level quality equivalence.

Post-timing traces on all four ranks confirm 24 Engram collectives removed over 12 forward steps. The peer gather itself is slower than a local gather; the benefit comes from removing the subsequent all-reduce. Profiled kernel intervals are not reported as endpoint speedups.

This remains draft. The DSPARK point estimates are positive, but five of six descriptive paired-bootstrap intervals include zero, all six paired log-ratio t intervals (df=3, sensitivity check) include zero, and several crossover blocks change sign. Non-speculative gains of +0.06% and +0.21% also reverse sign between the two startup pairs and are smaller than same-code startup drift. Stable incremental endpoint benefit over current main has not been established. The finite quality differences remain documented, without declaring either a proven regression or equivalence. Earlier measurements against ed89693 and local kernel improvements are not used to promote this PR. Lint and the updated title check pass; upstream GPU CI is gated by draft status, while the GPU validation above was run independently.

nodes.body: Thanks @BBuf! I believe main covers this now: #46180 added `--engram-config '{"lookup": "peer_read"}'`, which maps every TP peer's Engram shard (POSIX fds within a node, fabric handles across an NVLink domain) and reads each token's rows from the owner with one kernel, and #47033 makes it the default for GPU tables whose TP group is one NVLink domain, at any TP size and with or without DP attention. Closing as superseded; please reopen if I've missed a case.

+    TP_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
 ):
     row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
     idx = tl.load(ids_ptr + row).to(tl.int64)
     # The table holds rows [row_lo, row_hi); an id outside it is not read and
     # comes out as zeros, which is what the sharded all-reduce sums.
-    owned = (idx >= row_lo) & (idx < row_hi)

+        for rank in tl.static_range(TP_SIZE):
+            lower = tl.load(row_bounds + rank)
+            upper = tl.load(row_bounds + rank + 1)
+            match = (idx >= lower) & (idx < upper)
+            weight_address = tl.where(match, tl.load(w_ptr + rank), weight_address)
+            scale_address = tl.where(match, tl.load(s_ptr + rank), scale_address)
+            row_lo = tl.where(match, lower, row_lo)
+            owned |= match
+        w_ptr, s_ptr = weight_address, scale_address
+    else:
+        owned = (idx >= row_lo) & (idx < row_hi)
     local = tl.where(owned, idx - row_lo, 0)
     w = w_ptr.to(tl.int64).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.float8e4nv))
     s = s_ptr.to(tl.int64).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint8))

+"""Actual EngramEmbedding peer mapping, sharded lookup and graph reload parity."""
+
+import os
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.distributed import parallel_state as ps
+from sglang.srt.layers.engram import FP8_BLOCK_SIZE, EngramEmbedding
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_model
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.kernels.utils import multigpu_pytest_main
+from sglang.test.test_utils import publish_build_topology
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=90, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def group():
+    rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
+    world = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
+    local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
+    torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] != 10:
+        pytest.skip("Peer table integration is currently enabled only on SM10x")
+    ps.init_distributed_environment(
+        world_size=world,
+        rank=rank,
+        local_rank=local_rank,
+        distributed_init_method="env://",
+        timeout=180,
+    )
+    publish_build_topology(tp_size=world, world_rank=rank, device="cuda")
+    ps.initialize_model_parallel()
+    yield ps.get_tp_group()
+    ps.destroy_model_parallel()
+    ps.destroy_distributed_environment()
+
+
+def _reference(weight, scale, ids):
+    owned = (ids >= 0) & (ids < weight.shape[0])
+    safe = ids.clamp(0, weight.shape[0] - 1)
+    values = weight[safe].float().unflatten(-1, (256 // FP8_BLOCK_SIZE, FP8_BLOCK_SIZE))
+    values = (values * scale[safe].float().unsqueeze(-1)).flatten(-2)
+    return values.bfloat16().masked_fill(~owned.unsqueeze(-1), 0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("empty_shards", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("id_dtype", [torch.int32, torch.int64])
+def test_lookup_reload_and_graph(group, empty_shards, id_dtype):
+    bounds = [0, 1, 2, 3] if empty_shards else [0]
+    if not empty_shards:
+        for i in range(24):
+            bounds.append(bounds[-1] + 101 + i)
+    size = bounds[-1]
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    weight = torch.randn(size, 256, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    exponent = torch.randint(
+        120, 132, (size, 256 // FP8_BLOCK_SIZE), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8
+    )
+    exponent[0] = 0
+    scale = exponent.view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu)
+    with torch.device("cuda"):
+        peer = EngramEmbedding(size, 256, 1, tuple(bounds))
+    assert peer._peer_storage is not None
+    for overrides in ({"load_format": "dummy"}, {"weight_cache_mode": "client"}):
+        with torch.device("cuda"), get_model().override(**overrides):
+            assert EngramEmbedding(size, 256, 1, tuple(bounds))._peer_storage is None
+    peer._load_rows(peer.weight, weight)
+    peer._load_rows(peer.scale, scale)
+    peer.finish_load("test")
+    ids = torch.tensor(
+        [-1, 0, 1, size - 1, size, *bounds], device="cuda", dtype=id_dtype
+    ).view(-1, 1)
+    expected = _reference(weight, scale, ids)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(peer(ids), expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        peer(ids)
+    stream.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+        actual = peer(ids)
+    # Each rank issues distinct requests; peer lookup needs no forward collective.
+    torch.manual_seed(100 + group.rank_in_group)
+    ids.copy_(torch.randint(-1, size + 1, ids.shape, device="cuda", dtype=id_dtype))
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, _reference(weight, scale, ids), rtol=0, atol=0)
+    # A zero-token rank must not wait for other ranks' lookups.
+    local_ids = ids[: group.rank_in_group]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        peer(local_ids, cp_all_tokens=True),
+        _reference(weight, scale, local_ids),
+        rtol=0,
+        atol=0,
+    )
+    # Quiesce readers on every rank before mutating shared table storage.
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    torch.distributed.barrier(group=group.cpu_group)
+    # In-place reload preserves the captured peer addresses while updating values.
+    weight = (-weight.float()).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    peer._load_rows(peer.weight, weight)
+    peer.finish_load("reload")
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, _reference(weight, scale, ids), rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    torch.distributed.barrier(group=group.cpu_group)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    multigpu_pytest_main(__name__, __file__, num_gpus=(4,))

issue_comments.body: Thanks @BBuf! I believe main covers this now: #46180 added `--engram-config '{"lookup": "peer_read"}'`, which maps every TP peer's Engram shard (POSIX fds within a node, fabric handles across an NVLink domain) and reads each token's rows from the owner with one kernel, and #47033 makes it the default for GPU tables whose TP group is one NVLink domain, at any TP size and with or without DP attention. Closing as superseded; please reopen if I've missed a case.
